standard.title: Reflect on how identity is shaped by language and culture
standard.description: reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explain how language variation signals identity and social relationships, and how co-official languages relate to community identity (AC9LS8U04). They have not yet evaluated critically how language shapes belonging and exclusion, engaged in intercultural projects for real audiences, or reflected on language learning as identity experience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including belonging and exclusion, cultural change, and personal intercultural experience.

nodes.label: Language, belonging, exclusion and cultural change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how language choices create belonging or exclusion and reflect on how cultural change affects language and identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least one language feature creates belonging for some and exclusion for others; identify at least one example of cultural change affecting language or identity.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on how language choices signal group membership and cultural belonging; explore how jargon, slang and specialist language create inclusion and exclusion; reflect on how cultural change — migration, globalisation, digital culture — affects identity and language; explore assumptions in daily expressions; analyse how language changes with speakers' age, relationship and setting.
wider: Examine a target language community discourse where language choice signals belonging or exclusion — explain the mechanism and evaluate the social implications
Research how a significant cultural change has shifted language or identity in a target language community — explain the before and after, and what the shift reveals about the community's values
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding language as a vehicle for belonging and exclusion is the critical conceptual leap that moves cultural understanding from description to analysis. Students who only describe cultural practices cannot engage in evaluative reflection on language and power.

response_modes.reason: Belonging and exclusion analysis requires explicit evaluative frameworks — not only descriptive observation. Students need to articulate the mechanism by which language creates inclusion or exclusion.

success_criteria: Explains how at least one language feature creates belonging for some and exclusion for others
Identifies at least one example of cultural change affecting language or identity and explains the connection

nodes.label: Intercultural engagement and community projects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can engage in intercultural projects for real community audiences — exploring cultural knowledge and connections through genuine target language interaction.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute meaningfully to a community intercultural project using the target language — reflecting on the cultural exchange dimension.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in cultural exchanges with target language community peers; engage in pen-pal and collaborative project work; explore how Australians of target language community background navigate dual cultural identities; produce materials for cultural knowledge exchange; participate in reciprocal cultural sharing projects.
wider: Conduct a genuine intercultural exchange with a target language community peer — reflect on what was learned about both cultures from the exchange
Explore the experience of Australians who identify with both Australian and target language community backgrounds — present findings with cultural analysis in the target language

response_modes.reason: Intercultural community projects integrate all prior cultural understanding — belonging and exclusion (N1), language and identity — in a genuine exchange with real stakes and real cultural participants.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Genuine intercultural projects for real community audiences are the fullest expression of the entire language-and-culture learning journey. Students who have engaged in real cultural exchange understand the target language as a living community resource.
success_criteria: Contributes meaningfully to a community intercultural project using the target language
Reflects specifically on the cultural exchange dimension — not only the language production

nodes.label: Reflecting on language learning as identity experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on their own language learning experience as an identity experience — examining how learning a new language changes who they are and how they communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least two ways that learning the target language has changed how they communicate or see the world.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on the experience of moving between languages and cultures; consider the identity implications of being a language learner and a bilingual communicator; explore how language learning has changed their perspective on their own language; reflect on what intercultural competence means personally; consider future use of the target language.
wider: Write a reflective essay on the identity dimensions of their target language learning journey — connecting specific experiences to broader insights about language and identity
Consider how their experience as a language learner gives them specific insight into what it means to navigate between languages and cultures — and what this insight could offer in future contexts

response_modes.reason: Genuine personal reflection on language learning as identity requires students to move from reporting what they did to interpreting what it meant. Structured reflection frameworks scaffold the evaluative move from observation to interpretation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Reflecting on language learning as personal identity experience is the culminating act of the F-10 sequence — students who can articulate this reflection understand themselves as intercultural learners with genuine capabilities and perspectives.
success_criteria: Reflects on at least two ways that learning the target language has changed how they communicate or see the world
Connects specific language learning experiences to broader insights about identity and cultural understanding
